claim: zbus is a pure-Rust D-Bus API whose goal is to provide a safe and simple high- and low-level API akin to GDBus without depending on C libraries.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent can expose or consume D-Bus interfaces (systemd host info, login sessions) without pulling in libdbus C dependencies on every jupiterOS host
quoted_support: A Rust API for D-Bus communication. The goal is to provide a safe and simple high- and low-level API akin to GDBus, that doesn't depend on C libraries.

claim: zbus examples assume a D-Bus broker is set up and a session bus is running with DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS set, which is guaranteed on a typical Linux desktop session but NOT on headless hosts.
stance_target: a jupiterOS fleet agent running on headless kiosks/servers cannot assume a session bus; it must target the system bus or guarantee lingering + session bus per host
scope_conditions: headless Linux hosts, kiosks, servers without desktop sessions
quoted_support: Note that these examples assume that a D-Bus broker is setup on your machine and you've a session bus running (DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS environment variable must be set). This is guaranteed to be the case on a typical Linux desktop session.

claim: zbus server interfaces are defined by applying #[interface(name = ...)] to an impl block, and served via connection::Builder::session()?.name(...)?.serve_at(path, interface)?.build().await, testable externally with busctl --user call.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent could expose a D-Bus interface (e.g. org.jupiter.Agent1) with a straightforward macro-based pattern, verifiable via busctl in integration tests
quoted_support: #[interface(name = "org.zbus.MyGreeter1")] impl Greeter { fn say_hello(&mut self, name: &str) -> String ... } ... connection::Builder::session()?.name("org.zbus.MyGreeter")?.serve_at("/org/zbus/MyGreeter", greeter)?.build().await? ... $ busctl --user call org.zbus.MyGreeter /org/zbus/MyGreeter org.zbus.MyGreeter1 SayHello s "Maria"

claim: The zbus project is split into subcrates — zbus (API + wire format + name types), zbus_macros (#[proxy], #[interface], #[derive(DBusError)]), zbus_xml, zbus_xmlgen, zbus_utils — and dropped GVariant in favour of the sibling zgvariant project at 6.0.
stance_target: dependency footprint and versioning awareness for adding D-Bus to ha-linux-agent
quoted_support: zbus: The main subcrate. It provides the API to interact with D-Bus, the D-Bus wire format (what used to be the zvariant crate) and the name types ... zgvariant is a sibling project. It implements GVariant, the format zbus itself dropped in 6.0.
